positions.commentary: The speaker views Amphenol as a business to hold with conviction through obstacles and downturns, citing its proven pattern of enabling electrification, digitization, and new technologies.

thesis: This episode argues that Amphenol is a resilient, high-quality compounder with a culture of cost discipline and extraordinary diversification that acts as a natural shock absorber against industry-specific downturns. The speaker highlights the company's proven track record of organic growth, margin expansion, and disciplined capital deployment, noting its ability to compound earnings in the mid-teens annually over the past two decades. Additionally, the thesis posits that Amphenol is a prime beneficiary of structural trends like electrification, digitization, and the AI buildout, which drive content per unit and ensure a balanced earnings profile across various cycles.

claims.claim: Amphenol is a resilient, high-quality business with a culture of cost discipline and extraordinary diversification across end markets.
claims.quote: Amphenol has also, whether it's so many external shocks, whether that's being the dot-con collapse, the global financial crisis, COVID-19, the company has consistently emerged stronger compared to its peers.

claims.claim: Amphenol's extraordinary diversification ensures no single sector dominates, acting as a natural shock absorber against industry-specific downturns.
claims.quote: The most appreciated strength of Amphenol is its extraordinary diversification. Like many competitors that grew up serving one dominant industry, Amphenol has deliberately spread itself across the wide range of end markets.

claims.claim: Amphenol has a balanced, resilient earnings profile across various cycles due to its deliberate diversification strategy.
claims.quote: The diversification has never been scattershot. Amphenol's used acquisitions to deliberately strengthen weaker areas or expand into emerging technologies. And the result is a balanced, resilient earnings profile across various cycles.

claims.claim: Amphenol's content per unit rises as cars, factories, and servers become smarter and more electronic, driving structural growth.
claims.quote: That's the electrification, digitization, wave, impacting all markets. Every time a car, a factory, or a server becomes smarter and more electronic. Amphenol's content per unit rises. That's the flywheel of growth.

claims.claim: Amphenol is a trusted partner in the EV space, with content per vehicle rising much faster than overall car production due to electrification and assist systems.
claims.quote: So the battery pack alone can require dozens of rugged, high current interfaces that can safely handle up to a thousand volts. Add to that the growth driver of assist systems, radar, radar, camera sensors, all of which need reliable interconnects.

claims.claim: The speaker views Amphenol as a resilient, high-quality compounder with a strong track record of organic growth, margin expansion, and disciplined capital deployment, making it an exceptional company to hold through cycles.
claims.quote: We've owned Amphenol for over eight years, as it sits right in the sweet spot for how we invest. It was an exceptional company long before AI, and it will almost certainly remain an exceptional company once the AI cycle matures.

claims.claim: Amphenol has demonstrated exceptional resilience during downturns, with revenues falling only 13% during the global financial crisis compared to nearly 30% at peers, and maintaining operating margins when others plunged.
claims.quote: For example, during the global financial crisis, Amphenols revenues fell just 13 percent. That compares with nearly 30 percent at T connectivity. Then again in 2020, organic growth did to 1 percent growth, but operating margin remained 20 percent, whereas many industrial firms saw revenue declines and margins subsequently plunge.

claims.claim: Amphenol's financial history shows consistent compounding with revenues growing at a low double-digit rate over the past two decades, driven by roughly two-thirds organic growth and one-third from acquisitions.
claims.quote: So over the past, even just two decades, revenues have grown as a low double-digit rate. Roughly two-thirds of that growth has come organically averaging about seven percent, and the remaining third from acquisitions around five to six percent.

claims.claim: Amphenol has compounded earnings per share in the mid-teens annually over the past 20 years, reflecting top-line growth, steady margin expansion, and disciplined capital deployment.
claims.quote: Earnings per share have compounded even faster, and that's in the mid-teens annually. And that reflects obviously not just that top-line growth we've just mentioned, but steady margin expansion as well as the disciplined capital deployment.

claims.claim: Amphenol's operating margin has expanded from the mid-teens level to close to 25 percent over the past 20 years, consistently outpacing peers.
claims.quote: So over the past 20 years, Amphenols' operating margin has gradually expanded from the mid-teens level into that close to 25 percent range we see today, and that's consistently outpaced.

claims.claim: Amphenol generates a lot of cash, has steadily raised its dividend, and historically spends around 50 percent of free cash flow on M&A and 40 percent on buybacks.
claims.quote: Amphenols does generate a lot of cash, has steadily raised its dividend over time. The year remains modest at around 1 percent, but that's okay, because it's based upon a prioritization of acquisitions, which have historically offered very high returns, but it will also repurchase shares, if excess cash builds up, mainly to offset the delusion, rather than shrink the share account flow.
